name: Bidra Auctions for WooCommerce
author: BeautifulPlugins

sections.description:
Bidra Auctions for WooCommerce is a free WooCommerce auction plugin that adds a complete auction product type to your store. Create a listing, set a start price and an end time, and let your customers bid against each other. When the clock runs out the plugin picks the winner, emails them a payment link, and hands the order over to your normal WooCommerce checkout.

It is built the WooCommerce way: auctions are real products, so your theme, payment gateways, shipping rules, taxes, coupons and reports keep working exactly as they do today. It works with classic themes and block themes, the Cart and Checkout blocks, and High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).

Use it for online auctions, charity and fundraising auctions, and for selling collectibles, art, antiques, cars, equipment, livestock, domain names or liquidation stock — anything where buyers should name the price.

🚀 Upgrade to Pro | 💻 Live Demo Site | 📄 Plugin Documentation | 🎧 Support

Why store owners choose Bidra Auctions

  • Free and complete — a small store can run real auctions end to end without paying for anything.
  • Bidding that feels like eBay — quick-bid buttons, a bid confirmation step, live updates and a clear “You are winning” / “You have been outbid” status.
  • Runs itself — auctions open, close, pick the winner and send the emails on their own.
  • Light and private — no bundled libraries, no external requests, no tracking.

Everything you need to run a WooCommerce auction

  • Auction product type — a first-class WooCommerce product type, right next to Simple and Variable.
  • Start price and bid increment — decide where bidding opens and how much each new bid must add.
  • Reserve price — a hidden minimum. Bidders see whether the reserve is met, never the amount. An auction that ends below its reserve does not sell.
  • Buy It Now — let a buyer skip the auction and purchase immediately, and optionally withdraw the option once bidding starts.
  • Scheduled start and end times — line up auctions in advance and let them open and close on their own.
  • Automatic winner selection — when an auction ends, the highest bidder wins and is emailed a link to pay.
  • Winner-only checkout — nobody but the winning bidder can buy a finished auction.
  • End now, extend, restart — close an auction early, add time to it, or run it again from the product list. A restarted auction keeps its earlier bids as an archive.
  • Mark as sold — record a sale made outside the store.

A bidding experience customers understand

  • Live countdown timer on the auction page and, optionally, throughout your shop. It turns red when the auction is about to end.
  • Live bid updates — the current bid, minimum bid, bid count and the bidder’s own status refresh without a page reload.
  • Quick-bid buttons — one-click amounts under the bid field, in the shopper’s currency.
  • Bid confirmation — “Confirm your bid of $120?” inside the form, so a mistyped amount never becomes a bid.
  • Bid status badge — “You are winning”, “You have been outbid”, “You won” or “Not won” on the auction page, in the shop and in My Account.
  • Badges in product lists — Live, Starts soon, Ending soon, Ended, Sold, No reserve and Reserve met, each switchable, with colours you can change in one line of CSS.
  • Local time and Add to calendar — the end time in the visitor’s own timezone and an .ics reminder.
  • Auction terms — an optional “I agree to the auction terms” checkbox before a bidder’s first bid, with the consent date stored.
  • Bid history tab with every bid, the leading bid highlighted, and optional name masking for privacy.
  • Watchlist — customers save the auctions they care about; optionally show “12 people are watching this auction”.
  • My Account → Auctions with Active bids, Won (Pay now / Paid), Watchlist and Lost tabs.
  • Accessible — status changes are announced to screen readers, the bid form works from the keyboard, and reduced-motion preferences are respected.

Blocks, patterns and shortcodes

Seven blocks (search for “auction” in the block inserter), each with a live preview in the editor:

  • Auction grid — live, ending soon, upcoming or finished auctions, with columns, limit and category.
  • Auction countdown and Auction bid form — for one auction, or for the auction being viewed in a single product template.
  • Recent bids, My auctions, Auction watchlist and Auction status filter.

Three block patterns: Auction landing page, Ending soon strip and Upcoming auctions.

The single auction page works inside the WooCommerce block templates of block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five, and in classic themes such as Storefront.

Prefer shortcodes? Drop these into any page:

  • [bafw_auctions] — an auction grid. Accepts limit, columns, orderby, order, status and category.
  • [bafw_ending_soon_auctions], [bafw_future_auctions], [bafw_finished_auctions]
  • [bafw_my_auctions], [bafw_watchlist], [bafw_recent_bids]
  • [bafw_auction_status_filter] — Live / Upcoming / Ended links. Shop and category pages also accept ?auction_status=live, upcoming or ended.

Built-in email notifications

Every email uses the native WooCommerce email system, so it inherits your branding and can be customised or disabled under WooCommerce → Settings → Emails.

  • New bid placed (to you, and to the vendor on a marketplace)
  • You have been outbid (to the previous highest bidder)
  • You won the auction (to the winner, with a payment link)
  • Auction finished (to you)
  • Auction did not sell (to you)

Store tools

  • Setup wizard — creates the Auctions page, sets sensible defaults and can add a sample auction. Opens once on a new install; skippable.
  • WooCommerce → Auctions with Bids, Winners and Settings tabs: a searchable table of every bid, and who won what, for how much, and whether they have paid.
  • Dashboard widget — live auctions, auctions ending within 24 hours and wins awaiting payment.
  • CSV import and export — the auction fields are part of the WooCommerce product importer and exporter, so you can list auctions in bulk from a spreadsheet.
  • Duplicate an auction and get a clean copy: no bids, no winner, dates moved forward.
  • Google-friendly structured data — the current bid as the price, the end date as “price valid until” and the right availability.
  • Privacy tools — bids, watchlists and terms consent are part of the WordPress personal data export and erasure, with suggested privacy policy text.
  • Site Health checks — warns you when scheduled events, the timezone or a page cache could affect your auctions.
  • WP-CLI — wp bafw auctions list|close|restart and wp bafw bids list|delete.

Works with the plugins you already use

  • Dokan and WCFM Marketplace — auctions owned by a vendor work end to end: bids, vendor emails, checkout and commission.
  • CURCY – Multi Currency for WooCommerce — shoppers see prices and bid in their own currency; every bid is stored in your base currency, so everyone competes on the same ledger.
  • WooCommerce blocks, HPOS, taxes, coupons, shipping zones and every payment gateway.

Bidra Auctions Pro — for auction houses and marketplaces

The free plugin is a complete auction system. Bidra Auctions Pro adds the automation, auction types and auction-house tools that larger sellers ask for:

  • Proxy (automatic) bidding — bidders enter their maximum and the store bids for them, like eBay.
  • More auction types — sealed-bid (blind) auctions, reverse auctions (the lowest bid wins) and Dutch auctions (the price drops until someone buys).
  • Anti-sniping — bids in the final minutes extend the auction.
  • Auction events — timed sales with numbered lots, staggered closing, a catalog page, a printable catalog, event registration and results with CSV export.
  • Buyer’s premium — a percentage or fixed fee added to the winning bid at checkout, per store, event or auction.
  • Combined checkout and invoices — “Pay for all won auctions” in one order, and one invoice per bidder.
  • Bidder registration and approval, bidding (credit) limits and bidder (paddle) numbers.
  • Charity tools — fundraising goal with a progress bar, fair market value and receipt text in the winner’s email.
  • Pickup for won lots — local pickup only, pickup window and instructions.
  • Smart increments (percentage and tiered), bid retraction and bidder rules (block lists, account age, bid limits).
  • Automatic relisting, payment deadlines, second-chance offers and payment reminders.
  • Vendor auctions — Dokan and WCFM vendors create and manage their own auctions.
  • Extra emails (closing soon, payment reminder, reserve not met, relisted, bought now), reports with CSV export and a REST API.

See everything in Pro →

Developer friendly

  • Templates load through wc_get_template(), so your theme can override any of them in yourtheme/woocommerce/.
  • Documented actions and filters around bidding, auction lifecycle and display — see the Developer Documentation section below.
  • HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage) and Cart & Checkout Blocks compatible.
  • No bundled third-party libraries, no external requests and no tracking of any kind.

Perfect for

  • Charity, school and nonprofit fundraising auctions
  • Collectibles, coins, art, antiques and memorabilia dealers
  • Car, equipment, machinery and livestock sales
  • Estate sales, liquidation and clearance stores
  • Multivendor marketplaces built with Dokan or WCFM
  • Anyone who wants buyers to name the price

Privacy Policy

Bidra Auctions for WooCommerce stores the following data on your own server, and never transmits it anywhere:

  • Bids — the auction, the bidding user’s ID, the bid amount and the time it was placed, stored in the bafw_bids database table.
  • Watchlists — the IDs of the users watching each auction, stored as product meta.
  • Auction outcomes — the winning bidder’s user ID and the linked order, stored as product meta.
  • Auction terms consent — when you use the auction terms option, the date a user accepted them, stored as user meta.

The plugin makes no external HTTP requests, loads no remote assets, sets no cookies and includes no analytics or tracking of any kind. Bid data is retained until you delete the bid, delete the auction, or uninstall the plugin with the “Remove data on uninstall” setting enabled.

Developer Documentation

Constants

BAFW_VERSION, `BAFW_FILE`, `BAFW_PATH`, `BAFW_URL`, `BAFW_ASSETS_PATH`, `BAFW_ASSETS_URL`.

Helper functions

  • bafw_get_auction( $product ) — returns the AuctionProduct object, or false when the product is not an auction.
  • bafw_is_auction( $product ) — whether a product is an auction.
  • bafw_get_bidder_name( $user_id ) — the bidder name, masked when the setting is enabled.
  • bafw_get_max_bid_amount() — the configured single-bid ceiling.
  • bafw_get_account_auctions_url( $view ) — URL of a My Account auctions view.
  • bafw_local_to_timestamp( $date ) — convert a stored auction or bid date (site timezone) into a Unix timestamp.
  • bafw_format_date( $date ), bafw_format_duration( $seconds ) — display helpers.
  • bafw_get_template( $name, $args ), bafw_get_template_html( $name, $args ) — load a plugin template.

Actions

  • bafw_loaded — after the plugin has instantiated its classes.
  • bafw_installed — after installation or an upgrade routine completes.
  • bafw_before_place_bid — ( $auction, $amount, $user_id ) before a validated bid is stored.
  • bafw_bid_placed — ( $bid_id, $auction, $amount, $user_id ) after a bid is recorded.
  • bafw_bidder_outbid — ( $previous_bidder, $auction, $amount ) when a bidder is outbid.
  • bafw_bid_inserted — ( $bid_id, $data ) after a bid row is written.
  • bafw_bid_deleted — ( $bid_id, $bid ) after a bid row is removed.
  • bafw_auction_recalculated — ( $auction ) after an auction is rebuilt from its bids.
  • bafw_auction_started — ( $auction ) when bidding opens.
  • bafw_auction_closed — ( $auction, $winner_id, $fail_reason ) when an auction closes.
  • bafw_auction_won — ( $auction, $winner_id ) when an auction closes with a winner.
  • bafw_auction_failed — ( $auction, $fail_reason ) when an auction closes unsold.
  • bafw_auction_paid_state_changed — ( $auction, $paid, $order_id ).
  • bafw_watchlist_toggled — ( $auction_id, $user_id, $watching ).
  • bafw_before_bid_form / bafw_after_bid_form — ( $auction ) around the bid form.
  • bafw_product_data_panel — ( $auction ) at the end of the admin auction panel.
  • bafw_after_settings_fields — at the end of the settings form.
  • bafw_settings_saved — after the settings are saved.

Filters

  • bafw_validate_bid — ( $result, $auction, $amount, $user_id ) return a WP_Error to reject a bid.
  • bafw_minimum_bid — ( $minimum, $auction ) the lowest acceptable next bid.
  • bafw_bid_increment — ( $increment, $auction ).
  • bafw_max_bid_amount — ( $amount ) the single-bid ceiling.
  • bafw_can_bid_on_own_auction — ( false, $auction, $user_id ) allow sellers to bid on their own listings.
  • bafw_is_purchasable — ( $purchasable, $auction ).
  • bafw_is_buy_now_available — ( $available, $auction ).
  • bafw_cart_item_price — ( $price, $auction ).
  • bafw_price_html — ( $price_html, $auction ).
  • bafw_add_to_cart_text / bafw_add_to_cart_url — ( $value, $auction ).
  • bafw_bidder_name — ( $name, $user_id ).
  • bafw_item_conditions, bafw_auction_statuses, bafw_account_auction_views — the built-in option lists.
  • bafw_history_limit — ( 25 ) how many bids the history tab lists.
  • bafw_shortcode_query_args — ( $args, $atts ).
  • bafw_ajax_auction_data — ( $auctions, $auction_ids ) the live refresh payload.
  • bafw_auctions_per_cron_run — ( 50 ) how many auctions each cron run processes.
  • bafw_admin_tabs, bafw_screen_ids — extend the admin screens.

Templates

Copy any file from the plugin’s templates/ directory into yourtheme/woocommerce/ to override it, keeping the same relative path. For example, templates/single-product/auction-bid-form.php becomes yourtheme/woocommerce/single-product/auction-bid-form.php.

Support & Feedback

Found a bug or have an idea? Open a thread in the support forum or contact us directly.

Credits

Built and maintained by BeautifulPlugins.
sections.installation:
Requirements

  • WordPress 6.2 or newer
  • WooCommerce 7.0 or newer
  • PHP 7.4 or newer

Automatic installation

  1. Go to Plugins → Add New in your WordPress admin.
  2. Search for “Bidra Auctions for WooCommerce”.
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  4. The setup wizard opens: create the Auctions page, pick your defaults, and optionally add a sample auction. You can skip it and run it later from WooCommerce → Auctions → Settings.

Manual installation

  1. Download the plugin ZIP file.
  2. Go to Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  3. Choose the ZIP file and click Install Now, then Activate.

Creating your first auction

  1. Go to Products → Add New and give the product a title, description and image, exactly as you would for any other WooCommerce product.
  2. In the Product data dropdown, choose Auction.
  3. Open the new Auction tab and fill in the fields:
    • Item condition — optional label shown to bidders on the auction page.
    • Start price — the lowest amount the first bid may be.
    • Bid increment — the minimum amount each new bid must add to the current bid. Defaults to 1 when left empty.
    • Reserve price — optional hidden minimum. Bidders are told only whether the reserve has been met. An auction that ends below its reserve does not sell.
    • Buy It Now price — optional. Lets a buyer purchase immediately at this price. Leave empty to disable Buy It Now.
    • Auction starts — when bidding opens. Leave empty to start immediately.
    • Auction ends — when bidding closes and the highest bidder wins. Both dates use your site timezone.
  4. Publish the product.

The auction is now live on the product page, with a countdown timer, the current bid and the bid form. When the end time is reached the plugin closes the auction, marks the highest bidder as the winner and emails them a link to pay through your normal WooCommerce checkout.

Adding an auctions page

The setup wizard creates one for you. To build your own, create a page and add the Auction grid block (or the [bafw_auctions] shortcode), optionally with the Auction status filter block above it, then select the page under WooCommerce → Auctions → Settings → Auctions page.

Listing auctions in bulk

Go to Products → Import. Set the Type column to auction and add the columns “Auction start price”, “Auction bid increment”, “Auction reserve price”, “Auction Buy It Now price”, “Auction start date” and “Auction end date” (dates as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in your site timezone). Export a few auctions first to get a ready-made template.

Configuring the plugin

Store-wide rules live under WooCommerce → Auctions → Settings. The defaults work out of the box; adjust them as needed.

Catalog:

  • Auctions page — the page that lists your auctions.
  • Finished auctions — show or hide closed auctions on the shop and category pages.
  • Scheduled auctions — let shoppers preview auctions that have not opened yet.
  • Shop page — keep auctions off the main shop page so they are not mixed with regular products.

Bidding:

  • Maximum bid amount — the highest amount a single bid may be, to catch mistyped bids.
  • Buy It Now — keep Buy It Now available after bidding has started, or withdraw it with the first bid.
  • Raising your own bid — allow or block the current highest bidder from bidding against themselves.
  • Bidder privacy — mask bidder names in the public bid history, for example B*******e.
  • Watchlist — let customers save auctions, and optionally show how many people are watching.
  • Quick bids — show one-click bid amounts under the bid field.
  • Bid confirmation — ask bidders to confirm the amount before a bid is placed.
  • Auction terms — pick a page; bidders must agree to it before their first bid.

Display:

  • Countdown in product lists — show the countdown timer on shop and category pages.
  • Badges in product lists — choose which badges appear on auctions.
  • Ending soon — how many minutes before the end the countdown turns red and the “Ending soon” badge appears.
  • Local time — show auction times in the visitor’s timezone with an “Add to calendar” link.
  • Live bid updates and Update interval — refresh the current bid without reloading the page, and how often.

Advanced:

  • Remove data on uninstall — delete all auction data when the plugin is deleted. Off by default.

Auction emails are configured with the rest of your store emails under WooCommerce → Settings → Emails.

Managing your auctions

  • WooCommerce → Auctions → Bids — every bid ever placed, searchable and sortable, with single and bulk delete. Deleting a bid recalculates the auction from the bids that remain. Bids from before an auction was restarted are marked “Previous listing”.
  • WooCommerce → Auctions → Winners — who won what, for how much, and whether they have paid.
  • Products — an auction status column, a “filter by auction status” dropdown, and End auction now, Extend, Restart and Mark as sold actions.
  • Dashboard → Auctions widget — what is live, what ends today and what is waiting for payment.
  • My Account → Auctions — where your customers follow their bids, wins and watchlist, and pay for an auction they have won.
sections.faq:
Is this WooCommerce auction plugin really free?

Yes. The free plugin runs standard (ascending) auctions end to end: bidding, reserve price, Buy It Now, countdowns, live updates, watchlists, emails, winner checkout, blocks, shortcodes and the admin tools. Bidra Auctions Pro is an optional add-on for extra auction types, automation and auction-house features.

Does this work with my theme?

Yes. Auctions are ordinary WooCommerce products, so they use your theme’s product templates — classic themes and block themes alike. Every piece of auction markup lives in an overridable template under templates/, which you can copy into yourtheme/woocommerce/ and restyle. Badge and status colours are CSS custom properties, for example --bafw-badge-live-bg.

What happens when an auction ends?

A background task runs every minute and closes auctions whose end time has passed. The highest bidder becomes the winner and receives an email with a link to pay. If nobody bid, or the reserve price was not met, the auction is marked as unsold and you are notified instead.

What if WP-Cron is unreliable on my host?

The plugin also checks an auction’s state whenever its page is viewed or its live bid data is requested, so an auction always shows the correct status to a visitor even if the scheduled task is delayed. Tools → Site Health tells you when scheduled events are running late.

Does it work with page caching?

Yes. Live bid data is fetched from admin-ajax.php, which caches do not store by default. If you cache aggressively, exclude POST requests to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php; the Site Health check “Auction live updates” tells you when a cache is answering for the server.

Can I run a charity or fundraising auction?

Yes. Create your auctions, add the Auction grid block to a page, and take payment through your usual gateways. Bidra Auctions Pro adds auction events with a fundraising goal and progress bar, fair market value and receipt text for donors.

Can somebody else buy an auction that I won?

No. Once an auction closes, only the winning bidder can add it to the cart and check out.

Can the reserve price be seen by bidders?

No. Bidders are told only whether the reserve has been met.

Can I hide bidder names?

Yes. Enable Bidder privacy under WooCommerce → Auctions → Settings and names appear as the first and last character only, for example B*******e. Bidra Auctions Pro can show bidder (paddle) numbers instead.

Can I bid on my own auction?

No. Self bidding inflates the price artificially and is blocked by default. Developers can change this with the bafw_can_bid_on_own_auction filter.

Can I extend or restart an auction?

Yes. In the Products list or the Auction tab, use Extend to add time to a running auction (bids are kept) or Restart to run it again from now without bids, winner or order. The earlier bids stay in the Bids tab as a previous listing.

Does the plugin support automatic (proxy) bidding, sealed bids, reverse or Dutch auctions?

Those are part of Bidra Auctions Pro, together with anti-sniping, auction events with lots, buyer’s premium, bidder approval, automatic relisting and payment deadlines. The free plugin covers standard ascending auctions end to end.

Can I import auctions from a CSV file?

Yes. The auction fields are part of the WooCommerce product importer and exporter. Set the product type to auction and fill in the auction columns.

Does it work with currency switchers?

Yes. CURCY – Multi Currency for WooCommerce is supported out of the box: shoppers see auction prices and bid in their chosen currency, while every bid is stored in your store’s base currency so all bidders compete fairly. Other switchers can integrate through the bafw_display_amount and bafw_input_amount filters.

Does it work with Dokan or WCFM Marketplace?

Yes. Auctions owned by a vendor work end to end: bids, emails to the vendor, checkout and the vendor’s commission. In the free plugin the store admin creates the auction and assigns it to the vendor. With Bidra Auctions Pro, vendors create and manage their own auctions from their Dokan or WCFM dashboard.

Is it GDPR friendly?

The plugin stores bids, watchlists and terms consent on your own server and sends nothing anywhere. They are included in the WordPress personal data export, and an erasure request anonymises a user’s bids (the amounts stay in the auction history) and removes their watchlist and consent.

Will my data be deleted if I remove the plugin?

Only if you ask for it. Enable Remove data on uninstall in the settings before deleting the plugin, and the bid history, settings and auction meta are removed. Otherwise everything is left untouched.
sections.changelog:
1.3.0

  • New: Quick-bid buttons under the bid field — one-click amounts for the next bid, one increment further and four increments further, in the shopper’s currency.
  • New: Bid confirmation step (“Confirm your bid of …?”) shown inside the bid form before a bid is placed. On by default; switch it off in the settings.
  • New: Bid status badge — “You are winning”, “You have been outbid”, “You won” or “Not won” on the auction page, in product lists and in My Account, updated live.
  • New: Badges in product lists — Live, Starts soon, Ending soon, Ended, Sold, No reserve and Reserve met. Each can be switched off, and the colours are CSS custom properties (for example --bafw-badge-live-bg).
  • New: “Ending soon” urgency — the countdown turns red in the final minutes (60 by default, configurable).
  • New: Auction times in the visitor’s own timezone, and an “Add to calendar” (.ics) link.
  • New: Auction terms — choose a page and bidders must agree to it before their first bid; the date of consent is stored with their account.
  • New: My Account → Auctions now has Active bids, Won (Pay now / Paid), Watchlist and Lost tabs. Old links to the “My bids” and “Winning” views keep working.
  • New: Watcher count on the auction page (“12 people are watching this auction”). Off by default.
  • New: Bid flood protection — a bidder must wait two seconds between bids, which stops double submissions.
  • New: Seven blocks — Auction grid, Auction countdown, Auction bid form, Recent bids, My auctions, Auction watchlist and Auction status filter — and three block patterns.
  • New: The single auction page now renders inside the WooCommerce block templates of block themes (tested with Twenty Twenty-Five).
  • New: Auction status filter for shop and category pages: ?auction_status=live, upcoming or ended, with the [bafw_auction_status_filter] shortcode and block.
  • New: Setup wizard on a first-time install: creates the Auctions page, sets defaults and can add a sample auction as a draft. It never opens after an update; run it any time from the settings.
  • New: Auction fields in the WooCommerce product CSV importer and exporter.
  • New: Extend and Restart actions next to “End auction now”. A restarted auction starts a new listing: its earlier bids are kept under “Previous listing” in the Bids tab and no longer count.
  • New: Auctions widget on the WordPress dashboard: live auctions, auctions ending within 24 hours and wins awaiting payment.
  • New: Structured data for auctions — current bid, price valid until the end date, and availability.
  • New: Personal data exporter and eraser for bids, watchlists and terms consent, plus suggested privacy policy text.
  • New: Site Health checks for the auction scheduler, the site timezone, the auctions page and the live update endpoint.
  • New: WP-CLI commands: wp bafw auctions list|close|restart and wp bafw bids list|delete.
  • Fix: Duplicating an auction copied its bid count, winner, order and closed state. The copy is now a clean auction with its dates moved forward.
  • Fix: The countdown on the auction page did not follow a changed end time until the page was reloaded.
  • Fix: Bids were not removed when an auction was deleted through the REST API, WP-CLI or a vendor dashboard.
  • Tweak: Live updates fetch fresh data as soon as a countdown reaches zero or the shopper returns to the tab, and replace the bid form with an “ended” notice when the auction closes.
  • Tweak: The “outbid” email is only sent when the lead actually changes hands.
  • Dev: Bid listings — a listing column on the bids table, AuctionProduct::get_listing(), bafw_start_new_listing(), and a listing argument on Bids::query() / Bids::count().
  • Dev: Leading-bid hooks for add-on auction types: Bids::get_leading(), Bids::get_lowest(), AuctionProduct::get_bid_direction(), and the bafw_leading_bid, bafw_bid_direction, bafw_is_bid_amount_acceptable, bafw_bid_amount_error, bafw_is_reserve_met, bafw_buy_now_price, bafw_buy_now_sale_price and bafw_auction_price filters.
  • Dev: New actions bafw_auction_bought_now, bafw_auction_extended, bafw_auction_restarted, bafw_new_listing, bafw_auction_duplicated, bafw_terms_accepted, bafw_email_auction_details, bafw_account_auctions_before_table and bafw_account_auctions_view_{view}; new filters bafw_bid_status, bafw_auction_badges, bafw_quick_bids, bafw_quick_bid_multipliers, bafw_bid_flood_interval, bafw_account_auction_ids, bafw_recent_bids_query_args, bafw_csv_columns and bafw_structured_data_offer. The storefront script fires a bafw:auction-data DOM event with every live update.
  • Dev: New templates global/auction-bid-status.php, global/auction-status-filter.php and single-product/auction-watchers.php; updated templates (@version 1.3.0): the bid form, dates, countdowns, loop badge, bid history, My Account auctions and the “won” emails. Older copies in a theme keep working.

1.2.0

  • New: Dokan compatibility. Vendors get the “New bid”, “Auction finished” and “Auction failed” emails for their own auctions (new “Notify the vendor” setting on each email). When one checkout holds products from several vendors, the customer’s order settles the auction and Dokan’s vendor sub-orders are left alone, so the auction gets one order and one set of notes.
  • New: WCFM Marketplace compatibility. Vendors get the same auction emails for their auctions.
  • New: A vendor editing an auction in the Dokan or WCFM vendor dashboard can no longer turn it into a simple product or overwrite its price; the auction settings stay managed by the store admin (vendors can create and manage auctions with Bidra Auctions Pro).
  • Fix: Auctions created through the WooCommerce REST API (type: auction) were saved as simple products.
  • Tweak: The “you cannot bid on your own auction” rule now uses the auction’s seller, so marketplaces can map it to the store owner.
  • Dev: New AuctionData class — the single validate-and-save path for auction settings, used by the admin Auction tab and by vendor dashboards (bafw_auction_data_applied action, bafw_validate_auction_data filter).
  • Dev: bafw_get_auction_seller_id(), bafw_get_auction_vendor_id() and bafw_is_marketplace_active() helpers; bafw_auction_seller_id, bafw_auction_vendor_id, bafw_marketplace_active, bafw_auction_email_recipient, bafw_order_is_auction_source, bafw_dokan_vendor_auctions_enabled and bafw_wcfm_vendor_auctions_enabled filters. Auction emails now pass the auction to woocommerce_email_recipient_{id}.
  • Dev: Marketplace integrations live in includes/compat/dokan/ and includes/compat/wcfm-marketplace/ and only load when that plugin is active.

1.1.0

  • Fix: Currency symbols showed as HTML codes (for example ৳  or €) in the “Enter … or more” hint after the live bid update, in plain-text emails, in email subjects that use {auction_price} and in bid messages.
  • Fix: Auction prices now always follow the WooCommerce currency settings: symbol, symbol position, separators and decimals. The bid field shows the currency symbol and its step matches the store’s decimals.
  • Fix: Price labels in the Auction tab no longer show a stray space after some currency symbols, e.g. “Start price (৳ )”.
  • New: Compatibility with CURCY – Multi Currency for WooCommerce (free and premium). Auction prices, the bid form, bid history and Buy It Now are shown in the visitor’s currency; bids are converted back and stored in the store’s base currency, so everyone bids on the same ledger. Emails and admin screens use the base currency.
  • Dev: bafw_price(), bafw_price_text(), bafw_display_amount(), bafw_input_amount(), bafw_get_posted_bid_amount(), bafw_get_base_currency(), bafw_get_base_price_args() and bafw_get_currency_symbol() helpers, and the bafw_display_amount, bafw_input_amount, bafw_price_args, bafw_base_currency, bafw_base_price_args and bafw_curcy_convert_amount filters.
  • Dev: Third-party integrations now live in includes/compat/<plugin-slug>/ and load only when that plugin is active. Register your own with the bafw_compat_integrations filter; bafw_compat_loaded fires after each one boots.
  • Dev: Updated templates: the bid form, bid history, My Account auctions, recent bids, Buy It Now box and all emails (@version 1.1.0).

1.0.7

  • New: Added live demo site link for users to try the plugin before upgrading to Pro.

1.0.5

  • Fix: Buy It Now purchases made through the WooCommerce Checkout block did not close the auction, so it kept running and could be bought again. Paid orders created in the admin now close the auction too.
  • Fix: Sold auctions stayed “In stock”. A paid or sold auction is now set to “Out of stock”, and goes back in stock if its order is cancelled or refunded, or when the auction is reopened.
  • Fix: Saving an auction closed by Buy It Now no longer reopens it when its original end date is still in the future.
  • Fix: Guest Buy It Now purchases are now recorded as sold.
  • New: “End auction now” and “Mark as sold” actions in the Auction tab and the Products list, to close an auction early or record a sale made outside the store.
  • Dev: AuctionProduct::is_sold(), Scheduler::end_now(), Scheduler::mark_sold_offline() and the bafw_auction_sold_offline action.

1.0.4

  • Fix: Bidra Auctions Pro promotions are no longer shown when Pro is active.
  • Tweak: Admin notices are now shown to users who can manage options, and no longer depend on WooCommerce being active.

1.0.3

  • New: Admin notices for announcements and offers, with “Remind Me Later” and “Dismiss” options.
  • Tweak: Added Pro, documentation and support links to the plugin description.

1.0.1

  • Fix: Auction start and end times were shifted by the site’s UTC offset on sites whose timezone is not UTC, so auctions could open, close and display at the wrong time. Dates are now read in the site timezone.
  • New: bafw_local_to_timestamp() helper for converting auction and bid dates to timestamps.
  • Tweak: Updated the Pro feature list on the settings screen.

short_description: WooCommerce auction plugin: turn any product into a live auction with bidding, countdown timers, reserve price, Buy It Now and automatic winners.
description:
Bidra Auctions for WooCommerce is a free WooCommerce auction plugin that adds a complete auction product type to your store. Create a listing, set a start price and an end time, and let your customers bid against each other. When the clock runs out the plugin picks the winner, emails them a payment link, and hands the order over to your normal WooCommerce checkout.

It is built the WooCommerce way: auctions are real products, so your theme, payment gateways, shipping rules, taxes, coupons and reports keep working exactly as they do today. It works with classic themes and block themes, the Cart and Checkout blocks, and High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).

Use it for online auctions, charity and fundraising auctions, and for selling collectibles, art, antiques, cars, equipment, livestock, domain names or liquidation stock — anything where buyers should name the price.

🚀 Upgrade to Pro | 💻 Live Demo Site | 📄 Plugin Documentation | 🎧 Support

Why store owners choose Bidra Auctions

  • Free and complete — a small store can run real auctions end to end without paying for anything.
  • Bidding that feels like eBay — quick-bid buttons, a bid confirmation step, live updates and a clear “You are winning” / “You have been outbid” status.
  • Runs itself — auctions open, close, pick the winner and send the emails on their own.
  • Light and private — no bundled libraries, no external requests, no tracking.

Everything you need to run a WooCommerce auction

  • Auction product type — a first-class WooCommerce product type, right next to Simple and Variable.
  • Start price and bid increment — decide where bidding opens and how much each new bid must add.
  • Reserve price — a hidden minimum. Bidders see whether the reserve is met, never the amount. An auction that ends below its reserve does not sell.
  • Buy It Now — let a buyer skip the auction and purchase immediately, and optionally withdraw the option once bidding starts.
  • Scheduled start and end times — line up auctions in advance and let them open and close on their own.
  • Automatic winner selection — when an auction ends, the highest bidder wins and is emailed a link to pay.
  • Winner-only checkout — nobody but the winning bidder can buy a finished auction.
  • End now, extend, restart — close an auction early, add time to it, or run it again from the product list. A restarted auction keeps its earlier bids as an archive.
  • Mark as sold — record a sale made outside the store.

A bidding experience customers understand

  • Live countdown timer on the auction page and, optionally, throughout your shop. It turns red when the auction is about to end.
  • Live bid updates — the current bid, minimum bid, bid count and the bidder’s own status refresh without a page reload.
  • Quick-bid buttons — one-click amounts under the bid field, in the shopper’s currency.
  • Bid confirmation — “Confirm your bid of $120?” inside the form, so a mistyped amount never becomes a bid.
  • Bid status badge — “You are winning”, “You have been outbid”, “You won” or “Not won” on the auction page, in the shop and in My Account.
  • Badges in product lists — Live, Starts soon, Ending soon, Ended, Sold, No reserve and Reserve met, each switchable, with colours you can change in one line of CSS.
  • Local time and Add to calendar — the end time in the visitor’s own timezone and an .ics reminder.
  • Auction terms — an optional “I agree to the auction terms” checkbox before a bidder’s first bid, with the consent date stored.
  • Bid history tab with every bid, the leading bid highlighted, and optional name masking for privacy.
  • Watchlist — customers save the auctions they care about; optionally show “12 people are watching this auction”.
  • My Account → Auctions with Active bids, Won (Pay now / Paid), Watchlist and Lost tabs.
  • Accessible — status changes are announced to screen readers, the bid form works from the keyboard, and reduced-motion preferences are respected.

Blocks, patterns and shortcodes

Seven blocks (search for “auction” in the block inserter), each with a live preview in the editor:

  • Auction grid — live, ending soon, upcoming or finished auctions, with columns, limit and category.
  • Auction countdown and Auction bid form — for one auction, or for the auction being viewed in a single product template.
  • Recent bids, My auctions, Auction watchlist and Auction status filter.

Three block patterns: Auction landing page, Ending soon strip and Upcoming auctions.

The single auction page works inside the WooCommerce block templates of block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five, and in classic themes such as Storefront.

Prefer shortcodes? Drop these into any page:

  • [bafw_auctions] — an auction grid. Accepts limit, columns, orderby, order, status and category.
  • [bafw_ending_soon_auctions], [bafw_future_auctions], [bafw_finished_auctions]
  • [bafw_my_auctions], [bafw_watchlist], [bafw_recent_bids]
  • [bafw_auction_status_filter] — Live / Upcoming / Ended links. Shop and category pages also accept ?auction_status=live, upcoming or ended.

Built-in email notifications

Every email uses the native WooCommerce email system, so it inherits your branding and can be customised or disabled under WooCommerce → Settings → Emails.

  • New bid placed (to you, and to the vendor on a marketplace)
  • You have been outbid (to the previous highest bidder)
  • You won the auction (to the winner, with a payment link)
  • Auction finished (to you)
  • Auction did not sell (to you)

Store tools

  • Setup wizard — creates the Auctions page, sets sensible defaults and can add a sample auction. Opens once on a new install; skippable.
  • WooCommerce → Auctions with Bids, Winners and Settings tabs: a searchable table of every bid, and who won what, for how much, and whether they have paid.
  • Dashboard widget — live auctions, auctions ending within 24 hours and wins awaiting payment.
  • CSV import and export — the auction fields are part of the WooCommerce product importer and exporter, so you can list auctions in bulk from a spreadsheet.
  • Duplicate an auction and get a clean copy: no bids, no winner, dates moved forward.
  • Google-friendly structured data — the current bid as the price, the end date as “price valid until” and the right availability.
  • Privacy tools — bids, watchlists and terms consent are part of the WordPress personal data export and erasure, with suggested privacy policy text.
  • Site Health checks — warns you when scheduled events, the timezone or a page cache could affect your auctions.
  • WP-CLI — wp bafw auctions list|close|restart and wp bafw bids list|delete.

Works with the plugins you already use

  • Dokan and WCFM Marketplace — auctions owned by a vendor work end to end: bids, vendor emails, checkout and commission.
  • CURCY – Multi Currency for WooCommerce — shoppers see prices and bid in their own currency; every bid is stored in your base currency, so everyone competes on the same ledger.
  • WooCommerce blocks, HPOS, taxes, coupons, shipping zones and every payment gateway.

Bidra Auctions Pro — for auction houses and marketplaces

The free plugin is a complete auction system. Bidra Auctions Pro adds the automation, auction types and auction-house tools that larger sellers ask for:

  • Proxy (automatic) bidding — bidders enter their maximum and the store bids for them, like eBay.
  • More auction types — sealed-bid (blind) auctions, reverse auctions (the lowest bid wins) and Dutch auctions (the price drops until someone buys).
  • Anti-sniping — bids in the final minutes extend the auction.
  • Auction events — timed sales with numbered lots, staggered closing, a catalog page, a printable catalog, event registration and results with CSV export.
  • Buyer’s premium — a percentage or fixed fee added to the winning bid at checkout, per store, event or auction.
  • Combined checkout and invoices — “Pay for all won auctions” in one order, and one invoice per bidder.
  • Bidder registration and approval, bidding (credit) limits and bidder (paddle) numbers.
  • Charity tools — fundraising goal with a progress bar, fair market value and receipt text in the winner’s email.
  • Pickup for won lots — local pickup only, pickup window and instructions.
  • Smart increments (percentage and tiered), bid retraction and bidder rules (block lists, account age, bid limits).
  • Automatic relisting, payment deadlines, second-chance offers and payment reminders.
  • Vendor auctions — Dokan and WCFM vendors create and manage their own auctions.
  • Extra emails (closing soon, payment reminder, reserve not met, relisted, bought now), reports with CSV export and a REST API.

See everything in Pro →

Developer friendly

  • Templates load through wc_get_template(), so your theme can override any of them in yourtheme/woocommerce/.
  • Documented actions and filters around bidding, auction lifecycle and display — see the Developer Documentation section below.
  • HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage) and Cart & Checkout Blocks compatible.
  • No bundled third-party libraries, no external requests and no tracking of any kind.

Perfect for

  • Charity, school and nonprofit fundraising auctions
  • Collectibles, coins, art, antiques and memorabilia dealers
  • Car, equipment, machinery and livestock sales
  • Estate sales, liquidation and clearance stores
  • Multivendor marketplaces built with Dokan or WCFM
  • Anyone who wants buyers to name the price

Privacy Policy

Bidra Auctions for WooCommerce stores the following data on your own server, and never transmits it anywhere:

  • Bids — the auction, the bidding user’s ID, the bid amount and the time it was placed, stored in the bafw_bids database table.
  • Watchlists — the IDs of the users watching each auction, stored as product meta.
  • Auction outcomes — the winning bidder’s user ID and the linked order, stored as product meta.
  • Auction terms consent — when you use the auction terms option, the date a user accepted them, stored as user meta.

The plugin makes no external HTTP requests, loads no remote assets, sets no cookies and includes no analytics or tracking of any kind. Bid data is retained until you delete the bid, delete the auction, or uninstall the plugin with the “Remove data on uninstall” setting enabled.

Developer Documentation

Constants

BAFW_VERSION, `BAFW_FILE`, `BAFW_PATH`, `BAFW_URL`, `BAFW_ASSETS_PATH`, `BAFW_ASSETS_URL`.

Helper functions

  • bafw_get_auction( $product ) — returns the AuctionProduct object, or false when the product is not an auction.
  • bafw_is_auction( $product ) — whether a product is an auction.
  • bafw_get_bidder_name( $user_id ) — the bidder name, masked when the setting is enabled.
  • bafw_get_max_bid_amount() — the configured single-bid ceiling.
  • bafw_get_account_auctions_url( $view ) — URL of a My Account auctions view.
  • bafw_local_to_timestamp( $date ) — convert a stored auction or bid date (site timezone) into a Unix timestamp.
  • bafw_format_date( $date ), bafw_format_duration( $seconds ) — display helpers.
  • bafw_get_template( $name, $args ), bafw_get_template_html( $name, $args ) — load a plugin template.

Actions

  • bafw_loaded — after the plugin has instantiated its classes.
  • bafw_installed — after installation or an upgrade routine completes.
  • bafw_before_place_bid — ( $auction, $amount, $user_id ) before a validated bid is stored.
  • bafw_bid_placed — ( $bid_id, $auction, $amount, $user_id ) after a bid is recorded.
  • bafw_bidder_outbid — ( $previous_bidder, $auction, $amount ) when a bidder is outbid.
  • bafw_bid_inserted — ( $bid_id, $data ) after a bid row is written.
  • bafw_bid_deleted — ( $bid_id, $bid ) after a bid row is removed.
  • bafw_auction_recalculated — ( $auction ) after an auction is rebuilt from its bids.
  • bafw_auction_started — ( $auction ) when bidding opens.
  • bafw_auction_closed — ( $auction, $winner_id, $fail_reason ) when an auction closes.
  • bafw_auction_won — ( $auction, $winner_id ) when an auction closes with a winner.
  • bafw_auction_failed — ( $auction, $fail_reason ) when an auction closes unsold.
  • bafw_auction_paid_state_changed — ( $auction, $paid, $order_id ).
  • bafw_watchlist_toggled — ( $auction_id, $user_id, $watching ).
  • bafw_before_bid_form / bafw_after_bid_form — ( $auction ) around the bid form.
  • bafw_product_data_panel — ( $auction ) at the end of the admin auction panel.
  • bafw_after_settings_fields — at the end of the settings form.
  • bafw_settings_saved — after the settings are saved.

Filters

  • bafw_validate_bid — ( $result, $auction, $amount, $user_id ) return a WP_Error to reject a bid.
  • bafw_minimum_bid — ( $minimum, $auction ) the lowest acceptable next bid.
  • bafw_bid_increment — ( $increment, $auction ).
  • bafw_max_bid_amount — ( $amount ) the single-bid ceiling.
  • bafw_can_bid_on_own_auction — ( false, $auction, $user_id ) allow sellers to bid on their own listings.
  • bafw_is_purchasable — ( $purchasable, $auction ).
  • bafw_is_buy_now_available — ( $available, $auction ).
  • bafw_cart_item_price — ( $price, $auction ).
  • bafw_price_html — ( $price_html, $auction ).
  • bafw_add_to_cart_text / bafw_add_to_cart_url — ( $value, $auction ).
  • bafw_bidder_name — ( $name, $user_id ).
  • bafw_item_conditions, bafw_auction_statuses, bafw_account_auction_views — the built-in option lists.
  • bafw_history_limit — ( 25 ) how many bids the history tab lists.
  • bafw_shortcode_query_args — ( $args, $atts ).
  • bafw_ajax_auction_data — ( $auctions, $auction_ids ) the live refresh payload.
  • bafw_auctions_per_cron_run — ( 50 ) how many auctions each cron run processes.
  • bafw_admin_tabs, bafw_screen_ids — extend the admin screens.

Templates

Copy any file from the plugin’s templates/ directory into yourtheme/woocommerce/ to override it, keeping the same relative path. For example, templates/single-product/auction-bid-form.php becomes yourtheme/woocommerce/single-product/auction-bid-form.php.

Support & Feedback

Found a bug or have an idea? Open a thread in the support forum or contact us directly.
